title: Sauerbraten
subtitle: German braised pot roast in sweet-sour vinegar marinade
excerpt: Germany's national pot roast: beef marinated for days in vinegar, wine, and aromatics, then braised until meltingly tender in a sauce that balances sweet and sour, finished with dark raisins and crushed gingerbread.

recipe.sourceNotes: Sauerbraten (literally 'sour roast') is one of the most well-known German dishes internationally, often cited as the unofficial national dish of Germany alongside schnitzel. The dish is a pot roast that is marinated in a mixture of red wine vinegar, wine, onion, bay leaves, juniper berries, and cloves for two to seven days before cooking, which tenderises the beef and imparts a characteristic sour note. The braising liquid is then enriched with crushed Lebkuchen (gingerbread) or gingersnap biscuits to thicken and sweeten the sauce, creating the signature sweet-sour balance. The dish is traditionally served with potato dumplings (Kartoffelklösse) or Spätzle and red cabbage. A minimum three-day marinade is strongly recommended.

content.text: The minimum marinating time is 3 days; 5 to 7 days gives the most developed flavour and tenderness. Brown the meat very thoroughly before braising; the colour provides depth to the sauce. The gingerbread biscuits are the classic thickening agent; dark brown sugar is added at the end if the sweet-sour balance needs adjusting.

items.preparation: tied into a neat cylinder; topside or silverside also work
to balance the sweet-sour sauce; traditional recipes use crushed Lebkuchen but brown sugar works well

content.text: Combine the vinegar, wine, onion, carrot, bay, cloves, juniper, and peppercorns in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, cool completely. Pour over the beef in a non-reactive container. Refrigerate for 3 to 7 days, turning daily.

Remove the beef and pat dry. Reserve the marinade. Brown the beef all over in the oil in a large casserole over high heat. Remove. Cook the strained vegetables (onion and carrot) for 5 minutes. Return the beef. Pour in the strained marinade. Bring to a simmer, cover, and braise at 160°C / fan 140°C / gas 3 for 2.5 to 3 hours until very tender.

Remove the beef and rest. Strain the braising liquid. Return to the pan and stir in the crushed gingerbread biscuits and sultanas. Simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce is thick and glossy. Season and adjust the sweet-sour balance. Slice the beef and serve with the sauce.
